bestPractices.title: WebP Compression Best Practices
bestPractices.description: Follow these expert tips to get the best results from WebP compression.

tips.title: Leverage Dual Compression Modes
tips.content: Use lossless WebP for UI graphics, logos, and screenshots—typically 25% smaller than PNG. Use lossy WebP for photos at quality 80-90, achieving 25-35% better compression than JPEG with equal quality. WebP's alpha transparency compression is far superior to PNG's, especially for images with gradual transparency.

tips.title: Maximize Web Performance Gains
tips.content: WebP can reduce total page weight by 30-50% compared to JPEG/PNG. Prioritize conversion for large images (>100KB), hero images, and product photos. Use WebP's built-in sharpness parameter (0-7) to maintain perceived quality at lower file sizes. Consider WebP for responsive images to reduce mobile data usage significantly.

tips.title: Implement Progressive Enhancement
tips.content: WebP is supported by 95%+ of users (all modern browsers since 2020). Use <picture> element with WebP and JPEG/PNG fallback for universal compatibility. Avoid WebP for emails (limited email client support) and use JPEG/PNG for thumbnails in social media shares as platforms may not support WebP in all contexts.

tips.title: Strategic Batch Conversion
tips.content: Convert entire image libraries to WebP for consistent performance improvements. Use lossy quality 80-85 for content images, 85-90 for hero/featured images, and lossless for brand assets. Monitor visual quality on different devices—WebP's compression can appear different on various screens due to its advanced perceptual optimization.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.description: Common questions about WebP compression and our WebP compressor tool.

items.question: Is WebP better than JPEG?
items.answer: WebP typically provides 25-35% better compression than JPEG with similar or better quality, plus transparency support.

items.question: Do all browsers support WebP?
items.answer: Most modern browsers support WebP. For older browsers, you should provide fallback formats.

items.question: Should I use WebP for all images?
items.answer: WebP is great for web use, but consider your audience's browser support and provide fallbacks when necessary.

items.question: Is WebP secure to use?
items.answer: Yes, WebP compression happens entirely in your browser. Your images are processed locally and never uploaded to any server, ensuring complete privacy and security.
